The parameter type should be `DashboardWidgetSchema` instead of `any`. The `editSchema.widgets` array has type `DashboardWidgetSchema[]`. Using proper typing improves type safety.
```suggestion
        widgets: editSchema.widgets.filter((w: DashboardWidgetSchema) => w.id !== widgetId),
```

The parameter type should be `React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>` instead of `any`. This provides proper type safety and is the established pattern in this codebase (see AppManagementPage.tsx:151, ProfilePage.tsx:107, and other files). Using `any` defeats the purpose of TypeScript's strict mode and prevents catching potential bugs at compile time.

The parameter type should be `boolean` instead of `any`. The `onOpenChange` prop for Radix UI Dialog components expects `(open: boolean) => void`. Using `any` bypasses TypeScript's type checking unnecessarily.
```suggestion
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={(v: boolean) => { if (!v) dismiss(); }}>
```

The parameter type should be `React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>` instead of `any`. SidebarInput is built on top of the standard Input component, so it accepts the same event types. This is consistent with other Input onChange handlers in the codebase (e.g., AppManagementPage.tsx:151).
```suggestion
               onChange={(e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => setNavSearchQuery(e.target.value)}
```

The parameter type should be `UndoableOperation` instead of `any`. The `useGlobalUndo` hook's `onRedo` callback expects `(op: UndoableOperation) => void`. Import UndoableOperation from '@object-ui/core' for proper typing.

The parameter type should be `ConnectionStateEvent` instead of `any`. The `onConnectionStateChange` method expects `ConnectionStateListener`, which is `(event: ConnectionStateEvent) => void`. Import ConnectionStateEvent from './dataSource' to get proper type safety and IDE support for event properties like `state` and `error`.

The parameter types should be `DashboardWidgetSchema` for the widget parameter instead of `any`. The `editSchema.widgets` array has type `DashboardWidgetSchema[]`, so the map callback should be properly typed.

The parameter type should be `(prev: boolean) => boolean` instead of `(prev: any) => boolean`. The setter function for a boolean state expects the previous value to be a boolean. Using `any` is unnecessarily permissive.
```suggestion
    toggleDebug: () => setShowDebug((prev: boolean) => !prev),
```

The parameter should be typed as `ActionDef` instead of `any` to match the ActionRunner's handler signature. This would provide better type safety and IDE support for accessing action properties like `action.params`.

The parameter type should be `UndoableOperation` instead of `any`. The `useGlobalUndo` hook's `onUndo` callback expects `(op: UndoableOperation) => void` (see packages/react/src/hooks/useGlobalUndo.ts:20). Import UndoableOperation from '@object-ui/core' to get proper type safety and IDE support for operation properties like `description`.

The parameter type for the state setter should be `(prev: DashboardSchema | null) => DashboardSchema | null` instead of `(prev: any) => ...`. Since `editSchema` is typed properly elsewhere, maintaining consistent typing for state setters improves code quality.
```suggestion
      setEditSchema((prev: DashboardSchema | null) => {
```

The action parameter should be typed as `ActionDef` instead of `any`. The `registerHandler` method from ActionRunner expects `ActionHandler`, which is defined as `(action: ActionDef, context: ActionContext) => Promise<ActionResult> | ActionResult` (see packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:124-127). Using proper typing ensures type safety and IDE support for action properties.

The action parameter should be typed as `ActionDef` instead of `any`. The `registerHandler` method expects handlers with signature `(action: ActionDef, context: ActionContext) => Promise<ActionResult> | ActionResult`. Import ActionDef from the appropriate package to ensure type safety.

The parameter types should be properly typed instead of `any`. The state setter expects `(prev: DashboardSchema | null) => DashboardSchema | null`, and the widget array contains `DashboardWidgetSchema` items. Using proper types improves type safety.

The parameter type should be `React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>` or `React.MouseEvent` instead of `any`. The onClick handler for button elements receives a MouseEvent, and using proper typing helps catch potential issues.
```suggestion
                       onClick={(e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => { e.stopPropagation(); removeFavorite(item.id); }}
```

The parameter type should be `DashboardWidgetSchema` instead of `any`. The `schema.widgets` array has type `DashboardWidgetSchema[]` (see packages/types/src/complex.ts:567). Using proper typing provides better type safety and IDE support for widget properties.
